chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Aban ibn Uthman from Abu Basir who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): The people of Mecca criticized certain matters regarding you. He said: 'What are they?' I said: They said: 'You entered into ihram from al-Juhfa, while the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) entered into ihram from al-Shajara.' He said: 'Al-Juhfa is one of the two designated times (miqat), so I adopted the easier of the two for the people, and I was ill.'

key_terms.أَحْرَمَ: He entered into the state of ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.أَدْنَاهُمَا: The easier of the two (referring to the more accessible or less burdensome option)
key_terms.الْجُحْفَةُ: Al-Juhfa, a specific miqat location near Mecca
key_terms.الْشَّجَرَةُ: Al-Shajara, another miqat location near Mecca

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Sadiq enter ihram from al-Juhfa instead of al-Shajara?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that al-Juhfa is one of the two primary miqat locations, and he chose it as the closer option for the residents of Mecca, noting his own illness as a factor in his specific practice. This narration highlights the scholarly principle of facilitating religious obligations (taysir) based on geographic proximity and individual circumstances, a key theme in Shia fiqh regarding Hajj rituals. It also underscores the authority of the Imams in interpreting and applying the Prophet’s traditions with precision.
